newsitem.title: australia: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: ANDREWS BILL COULD BE ENACTED TODAY
The Andrews bill over-riding the Northern Territory's voluntary euthanasia laws could be enacted as early as today.
There've been calls to delay its enactment to allow two terminally ill patients in the Territory to use the right-to-die law to end their lives.
Parliamentary officials in Canberra say the Andrews bill could go before the Governor-General for Royal Assent before the end of the day.
The bill was passed by the Senate overnight, 38 votes to 33.
HIGHER PENALTIES FOR SPEEDING IN NEW SOUTH WALES

Motorists travelling in New South Wales over the Easter break could lose their licence if they go over the speed limit. The New South Wales Government is doubling the demerit points for speeding as a short-term safety measure over Easter.
The increase will take effect from midnight tonight until midnight next Monday.
Drivers exceeding the speed limit by more than 45 kilometres an hour will lose 12 demerit points and automatically lose their licence for six months.
All other driving offences will have an extra demerit added to the penalty.
Nearly two-thousand extra police will be on duty for the Easter period.
BANK CLOSURES CAUSE LOST CONFIDENCE - SURVEY FINDS
A new survey has revealed the closure of country banks has contributed to the decline of small towns.
The University of Southern Queensland study found as many as one thousand banks have closed in country towns around Australia since 1993.
Economics lecturer Deborah Ralston says this is despite official figures showing 322 country banks have closed.
She says the closures are creating a financial drain on the communities and eroding local confidence in the future.
CYCLONE JUSTIN A THING OF THE PAST - MOST LIKELY
It appears ex-tropical cyclone Justin, which has had a serious impact on North Queensland and Papua New Guinea for about three weeks, has finally gone.
It was responsible for a number of deaths, flooding and wind damage across a widespread area, and the weather bureau's David Alexander says the system will weaken further in the next two days.
The significant tropical low is now 100 kilometres north-east of Mackay, and he says conditions aren't suitable for Justin to reform.
CARR URGES PM TO GO FOR MINIMALIST REPUBLIC
New South Wales Premier Bob Carr says while Australia becoming a republic is not a huge issue, he believes the time for change is right, and is something that most Australians want.
Mr Carr has revealed he's privately urged Prime Minister John Howard to use his authority to lead Australia towards a minimalist Republic, before last week's Premier's conference.
Mr Carr says it would be a great thing to have Australia led towards this inevitable re-arrangement by a Conservative leader, who could carry the part of Australia which still resists the idea.
But the Prime Minister replied he thought Australia was a Republic in all but name.
And Australians for a Consitutional Monarchy say the Premier should leave it up to the Government's convention to decide.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
